title: Regression in query building when using union and with_entities

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

labels.name: with_entities change
labels.description: issues related to the altered behvaior of Query w/ 1.4/2.0

body:
**Describe the bug**
Since version 1.4.19 (in particular commit https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/5b3e887f46afdbee312d5efd2a14f7c9b7eeac65 fixing https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6503 and https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6253 ) the behavior when generating queries using union seems wrong. I'm not 100% sure it's because of the union, but this is the case I ran into. Version 1.4.18 worked fine.

**To Reproduce**
```py
import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, sessionmaker

DeclarativeBase = declarative_base()
Session = sessionmaker()
session = Session()


class Parent(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "parent"
    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)


class EventInvitation(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey("parent.id"))
    parent = relationship(Parent)


class EventResponse(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "b"

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey("parent.id"))
    parent = relationship(Parent)


parent_id = 1
x = (
    session.query(EventInvitation)
    .filter(EventInvitation.parent_id == parent_id)
    .outerjoin(EventResponse, (EventResponse.parent_id == EventInvitation.parent_id))
    .with_entities(EventInvitation, EventResponse)
)
y = (
    session.query(EventResponse)
    .filter(EventResponse.parent_id == parent_id)
    .outerjoin(EventInvitation, (EventInvitation.parent_id == EventResponse.parent_id))
    .with_entities(EventInvitation, EventResponse)
)
print("UNION")
print(x.union(y))
print("UNION+COUNT (simulate x.union(y).count()")
print(x.union(y)._from_self(sa.sql.func.count(sa.sql.literal_column("*"))).enable_eagerloads(False))

```

**Output**
This is the correct output using 1.4.18:

```sql
# BEFORE, UNION
SELECT 
  anon_1.a_id AS anon_1_a_id, anon_1.a_parent_id AS anon_1_a_parent_id, anon_1.b_id AS anon_1_b_id, anon_1.b_parent_id AS anon_1_b_parent_id 
FROM 
  (
    SELECT 
      a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
    FROM  a
    LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON b.parent_id = a.parent_id 
    WHERE 
      a.parent_id = : parent_id_1 
    UNION 
    SELECT 
      a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
    FROM b 
      LEFT OUTER JOIN a ON a.parent_id = b.parent_id 
    WHERE 
      b.parent_id = : parent_id_2
  ) AS anon_1

# BEFORE, UNION+COUNT
SELECT 
  count(*) AS count_1 
FROM 
  (
    SELECT 
      anon_2.a_id AS anon_2_a_id, anon_2.a_parent_id AS anon_2_a_parent_id, anon_2.b_id AS anon_2_b_id,  anon_2.b_parent_id AS anon_2_b_parent_id 
    FROM 
      (
        SELECT 
          a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
        FROM a 
          LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON b.parent_id = a.parent_id 
        WHERE 
          a.parent_id = : parent_id_1 
        UNION 
        SELECT 
          a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
        FROM b 
          LEFT OUTER JOIN a ON a.parent_id = b.parent_id 
        WHERE 
          b.parent_id = : parent_id_2
      ) AS anon_2
  ) AS anon_1

```

This is the incorrect output using the commit referenced above included in 1.4.19
```sql
# AFTER, UNION
SELECT 
  anon_1.a_id AS anon_1_a_id,   anon_1.a_parent_id AS anon_1_a_parent_id,   anon_1.b_id AS anon_1_b_id,   anon_1.b_parent_id AS anon_1_b_parent_id 
FROM 
  (
    SELECT 
      a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
    FROM       a 
      LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON b.parent_id = a.parent_id 
    WHERE 
      a.parent_id = : parent_id_1 
    UNION 
    SELECT 
      a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
    FROM       b 
      LEFT OUTER JOIN a ON a.parent_id = b.parent_id 
    WHERE 
      b.parent_id = : parent_id_2
  ) AS anon_1 
  LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON anon_1.b_parent_id = anon_1.a_parent_id


# AFTER, UNION+COUNT
SELECT 
  count(*) AS count_1 
FROM 
  (
    SELECT 
      anon_2.a_id AS anon_2_a_id,       anon_2.a_parent_id AS anon_2_a_parent_id,       anon_2.b_id AS anon_2_b_id,       anon_2.b_parent_id AS anon_2_b_parent_id 
    FROM 
      (
        SELECT 
          a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
        FROM a 
          LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON b.parent_id = a.parent_id 
        WHERE 
          a.parent_id = : parent_id_1 
        UNION 
        SELECT 
          a.id AS a_id, a.parent_id AS a_parent_id, b.id AS b_id, b.parent_id AS b_parent_id 
        FROM b 
          LEFT OUTER JOIN a ON a.parent_id = b.parent_id 
        WHERE 
          b.parent_id = : parent_id_2
      ) AS anon_2 
      LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON anon_2.b_parent_id = anon_2.a_parent_id
  ) AS anon_1 
  LEFT OUTER JOIN b ON anon_1.anon_2_b_parent_id = anon_1.anon_2_a_parent_id

```

Note in the incorrect case a stray LEFT OUTER JOIN being added at the end of the query, presumably from the first part of the UNION, and in the second case, the LEFT OUTER JOIN is being added yet another time to the count query. Sometimes the query happens to be valid, other times the query is invalid because some columns are not referencable from there. This particular case made one of our query jump from a few milisecs, to several minutes 🤯 

My guess is that the memoization gets applied erroneously in the UNION case, and results in part of the memoization applying to the outside of the UNION, but ???

**Versions.**
 - OS: OSX
 - Python: 3.9
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4.18 (OK) 1.4.19-20 (NOK)

Thanks a lot !
